deals.whyRanked: Fresh United fare posted just yesterday at $141 RT basic economy — down sharply from the $222 we saw here days ago — and Rocky Mountain National Park is 90 minutes away via Estes Park.
deals.soloWhy: The A Line train runs straight from DEN into downtown, LoDo and RiNo are walkable, and the outdoor-gear/hostel crowd makes it easy to link up for a day hike solo.

highlights: Golden, CO and the Colorado Railroad Museum
Clear Creek whitewater park in Golden
Chautauqua Park and the Flatirons in Boulder
itinerary: Day 1 — A Line into downtown, wander Union Station and Larimer Square, dinner in RiNo.
Day 2 — Day trip to Boulder: hike the Chautauqua Trail up to the Flatirons (moderate, 3 mi RT), lunch on Pearl Street.
Day 3 — Golden for the School of Mines campus and Clear Creek, or push further to Rocky Mountain NP's Bear Lake corridor if you have a car.
guide.gettingAround: A Line train covers the airport-to-downtown hop for free walking around; you'll want a rental car for Boulder, Golden, or the national park.
guide.stayArea: RiNo or LoDo — both walkable, close to breweries and the train line.
food: The Post Brewing Co. (Boulder day trip)

deals.travelWindow: Sep 12 – Dec 12, limited Saturday nonstop fares (American)
deals.whyRanked: The cheapest verified fare of the five at $131 RT nonstop, though it's a Saturday-only basic-economy fare and there's no national park nearby.
deals.soloWhy: Bishop Arts District and the Katy Trail are walkable and low-key, but Dallas sprawls — a rideshare or the DART rail is needed to cover the rest.

highlights: Dallas Museum of Art (free general admission)
The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza
Katy Trail for a morning walk or run
itinerary: Day 1 — Klyde Warren Park, Dallas Museum of Art, dinner in the Arts District.
Day 2 — Bishop Arts District for boutiques and tacos, evening on the Katy Trail.
Day 3 — The Sixth Floor Museum and Reunion Tower before an afternoon flight.
guide.gettingAround: DART light rail connects downtown to Bishop Arts and Mockingbird Station; a rental car opens up the rest of the metro.
guide.stayArea: Downtown or Uptown — closest to the DART line and walkable restaurant rows.

deals.travelWindow: Fall 2026, nonstop JetBlue basic economy fares fluctuating in this range
deals.whyRanked: $197–267 RT nonstop on recent JetBlue fare drops, and the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area (Malibu Creek, Topanga) is a 30–45 minute drive from the Westside.
deals.soloWhy: Santa Monica, Venice and Downtown's Arts District are walkable pockets, but LA is car-dependent between them — budget for rideshares or a rental.

highlights: Griffith Observatory and the Hollywood sign trails
itinerary: Day 1 — Santa Monica Pier, walk or bike the Venice Boardwalk, sunset at Abbot Kinney.
Day 2 — Griffith Park: hike to the Observatory, then Grand Central Market and the Arts District downtown.
Day 3 — Rent a car for the morning and hike Malibu Creek State Park or Solstice Canyon before an afternoon flight.
guide.gettingAround: The Metro E Line reaches Santa Monica from downtown, but a rental car or regular rideshares are the practical way to see Griffith Park, Malibu, or Joshua Tree.
guide.stayArea: Santa Monica or Venice — walkable to the beach and easiest to explore without a car for a day or two.
food: Erewhon (for the people-watching as much as the food)

deals.travelWindow: Fall 2026, nonstop Alaska and JetBlue basic economy fares in this range
deals.whyRanked: $207–257 RT nonstop, and Cabrillo National Monument sits right in the city — a solo-friendly downtown with a national park unit a 15-minute drive away is a rare combination.
deals.soloWhy: Compact, walkable Gaslamp and Balboa Park, a trolley that actually covers the tourist core, and Torrey Pines' well-trafficked trails make solo hiking feel safe.

highlights: Cabrillo National Monument tide pools and lighthouse
itinerary: Day 1 — Balboa Park museums and gardens, dinner in the Gaslamp Quarter.
Day 2 — Point Loma: Cabrillo National Monument tide pools and lighthouse, afternoon in Old Town.
Day 3 — Hike Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve, then La Jolla Cove before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The MTS trolley and buses cover downtown, Balboa Park and Old Town well; a car or rideshare is worth it for Point Loma and Torrey Pines.
guide.stayArea: Gaslamp Quarter or Little Italy — walkable to the trolley and the harbor.

deals.whyRanked: The priciest of the five at $297 RT nonstop, but Olympic and Mount Rainier National Parks are both within a couple hours and Seattle is one of the most solo-friendly big cities in the country.
deals.soloWhy: Link light rail runs straight from SEA into downtown, Pike Place and Capitol Hill are made for wandering alone, and the hostel and coffee-shop culture makes it easy to strike up conversation.

highlights: Kerry Park views of the skyline
Ferry ride across Elliott Bay to Bainbridge Island
itinerary: Day 1 — Link light rail into downtown, Pike Place Market, Kerry Park at sunset.
Day 2 — Ferry to Bainbridge Island for the day, or Discovery Park's Loop Trail if you'd rather stay in the city.
Day 3 — Rent a car for a Mount Rainier day trip (Paradise area for the wildflower meadows) or push to Olympic NP's Hurricane Ridge.
guide.gettingAround: Link light rail covers the airport-to-downtown trip and most of the city core; a rental car is worth it only for the national park days.
guide.stayArea: Capitol Hill or Belltown — walkable, close to transit and nightlife.
